info.title: ZapSMTP API
info.description: Send, receive and track email. Docs: https://zapsmtp.com/docs/

tags.name: Emails
tags.description: Send one email or up to 100 in a batch, schedule them, and follow every recipient from acceptance to the remote server’s reply. Sending to …@simulator.zapsmtp.com with a test key runs the whole pipeline without delivering anything.

tags.name: Domains
tags.description: Add the domain you send from, publish the DNS records it returns (DKIM, SPF, DMARC) and verify it. Live keys can only send from verified domains.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: Register an HTTPS endpoint and choose events. Every request is signed; see Webhook events for payloads and signature verification. filter.actions narrows email.clicked to some click actions.

tags.name: Click actions
tags.description: Mark a link with data-zap-action="confirm_order" and its clicks arrive as email.clicked with click.action; a webhook can take only the actions you list in filter.actions. Declaring an action here is optional: it gives it a description. The catalogue also lists the actions links used without one. See the Click actions guide.

tags.name: Templates
tags.description: Edit a draft, then publish it: sends always use the published version, so changes go live only when you say so. Templates use logic-less Mustache: {{name}} is escaped, {{{html}}} is raw, sections repeat over lists. Send with template: {id, variables} on Send an email; variable_schema declares each variable’s type, whether a send must give it and its default (see Variables). Every save is kept in the version history (the newest 50), ready to restore.

tags.name: Variables
tags.description: One list of every variable your templates can use: ZapSMTP’s own ({{{zap:unsubscribe_url}}}), the account’s global ones ({{global.company_name}}, set here and never by a send) and each template’s own, with where each is used. See Variables in the templates guide.

tags.name: Modules, images & timers
tags.description: What the visual editor shares across templates: modules (saved rows any template can insert), images hosted on a public URL, and countdown timer images. All of it works through the API too.

tags.name: Received emails
tags.description: Messages sent to your inbound addresses land here. The email.received webhook carries metadata only; fetch bodies and attachments with these endpoints.

tags.name: Inbound setup
tags.description: Get an instant managed address or receive on your own domain, then route messages by recipient, sender or header to a webhook, storage or rejection.

tags.name: Suppressions
tags.description: Permanent mailbox or domain failures, complaints and one-click unsubscribes add an address here automatically. Sends to a suppressed address are skipped and reported as email.suppressed. An unsubscribe stops only broadcast email; transactional email to that address still goes out.

tags.name: Statistics
tags.description: Counts for the window you ask for, limited to your plan’s log retention.

tags.name: API keys & SMTP credentials
tags.description: Use separate keys per application and environment. Test keys (zap_test_…) run the full pipeline without delivering. SMTP credentials have their own username and password and never authorize the HTTP API.

tags.name: Logs, usage & account
tags.description: Find out exactly what your code sent and what we answered. Every response’s X-Request-Id is the id of its log entry.

tags.name: Simulator & dedicated IPs
tags.description: List the simulator scenarios and your dedicated IPs with their warm-up and blocklist status.

post.description: Send an email (or schedule it with scheduled_at). Requires a full-access or sending-access key. Live keys: From domain must be verified by the account. Test keys: any From domain, nothing delivered, monthly quota not charged. Recipients are deduplicated and lowercased; max 50 across to+cc+bcc. Message-ID is <id>@<hostname>, or <id>.<thread_id>@<hostname> for a reply that continues a conversation. The response also carries thread_id: the conversation this email belongs to. An email with In-Reply-To / References headers (set them in headers) joins the thread of the message it answers; otherwise it starts a new one. failed_recipients: addresses the mail server refused while it took the others; they are not sent and not charged. unconfirmed: true: the mail server took the message but its answer was lost; it counts as sent and must not be retried (its events tell the outcome). Scheduled emails (scheduled_at): at most 10,000 (256 MB) may wait per account. At send time the account and the key are checked again: a suspended account or a revoked or expired key fails the email. With reply tracking on, the response carries reply_to: the tracked address the email carries in place of its own Reply-To. Human replies are forwarded to the domain’s reply_forward_to, else to the email’s first Reply-To, else to its From.

patch.description: Set the domain's tracking defaults (opens, clicks, replies) and its outbound TLS policy. Requires a full-access live key; test keys get 403 test_key_restricted. Fields left out keep their value. The response is the domain, as in GET /domains/{id}. Reply tracking: each tracked email gets its own signed Reply-To, e.g. r1-<email id>.<signature>@reply.acme.com, so replies come back tied to the exact email. Each reply fires email.replied (classified as a person, out-of-office, unsubscribe request, bounce…) and arrives as a received email; only replies a person wrote are forwarded. The display name is kept (the Reply-To’s name, else the From name). One reply address takes at most 100 replies a day.
